studies.title: Health-related quality of life in women and men with long COVID.
studies.authors: Garces-Arilla, Sara, Fidalgo, Camino, Mendez-Lopez, Magdalena, Hidalgo, Vanesa et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is associated with persistent physical and emotional symptoms that may substantially impair health-related quality of life, with growing evidence suggesting that these outcomes differ between women and men. This cross-sectional study examined sex differences in health-related quality of life, lifestyle habits, and symptom severity in long COVID, and explored factors associated with health-related quality of life in women and men. A total of 342 adults with long COVID (mean age = 51.20 years, SD = 10.49; 265 women and 77 men) completed a battery of questionnaires during a single, face-to-face individual assessment session. The questionnaires assessed health-related quality of life, smoking behaviour, physical activity, dyspnoea, fatigue, and anxiety and depressive symptoms. Controlling for age and months since diagnosis, women reported lower quality of life and greater dyspnoea severity than men, whereas no sex differences were observed in smoking behaviour, fatigue severity, or anxiety and depressive symptoms. In sex-stratified exploratory analyses, poorer quality of life was associated with greater dyspnoea, fatigue, and emotional symptom severity in women, whereas in men it was associated with greater fatigue. However, interactions between sex and these factors were not statistically significant. These findings indicate sex differences in health-related quality of life and dyspnoea severity among individuals with long COVID. Larger, adequately powered studies are needed to determine whether the factors associated with health-related quality of life differ by sex.

studies.title: Post-acute infection: before we forget it again.
studies.authors: Madsen, Helena Borland, Desler, Claus
studies.abstract: Long COVID did not invent the post-acute phase of infection; it made it impossible to ignore. Acute infections are still often framed as time-limited events that end in recovery, deterioration or death, but this view fails to capture patients who remain biologically and clinically unwell after the acute infection has passed. The problem extends beyond SARS-CoV-2. Post-acute morbidity has been described after influenza, Epstein-Barr virus infection, Q fever, sepsis, and other infections, yet definitions, coding systems, and clinical pathways remain fragmented. We argue that post-acute infection should not be organized only by the initiating pathogen. Such pathogen-centric labels may be clinically tidy, but they risk producing heterogeneous cohorts, diluted biomarker signals, and disease-specific silos that obscure shared mechanisms of incomplete recovery. Instead, the field needs a second axis: the host-recovery state. Persistent inflammation, immune remodelling, loss of tolerance, antigenic stimulation, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial impairment, and tissue injury may represent overlapping immunometabolic failure modes across infections. Defining these states over time could help transform post-acute infection from a residual clinical label into a mechanism-informed framework for research, biomarkers, and care.

studies.title: Neurocognitive Indices of Long COVID: Dysregulated Engagement of Inhibitory Control and Oscillatory Slowing.
studies.authors: White, David R, Parker, Katie S, Marinkovic, Ksenija
studies.abstract: Persistent neurocognitive symptoms, such as "brain fog", insomnia, or fatigue, are prevalent in PASC (post-acute sequelae of COVID-19, "Long COVID"), even after mild acute illness. However, evidence for the neural underpinnings of cognitive dysregulation and altered spontaneous neural activity is inadequate. EEG data were acquired during an inhibitory Go/NoGo task and wakeful rest from young, otherwise healthy adults with PASC approximately six months after recovery from mild COVID-19. Neurobehavioral indices were computed for correct and erroneous trials, resting state, and the questionnaire battery, and compared with a matched control (CONT) group of individuals not exposed to COVID-19. The PASC group reported higher cognitive difficulties, anxiety, depression, and sleep problems, consistent with the known symptomatic pattern. Despite intact task performance, neural indices indicated altered engagement of cognitive control in the PASC group on both correct and error trials, which was associated with less efficient responding. Moreover, co-oscillatory synchrony trended toward dysregulation during error commission in the PASC group. Altered neural indices of inhibitory control marginally correlated with spontaneous oscillatory slowing, potentially suggesting shared basic mechanisms. The overall pattern of PASC symptoms, altered neural activity during inhibitory control, and oscillatory slowing, is indicative of the core neural dysfunction characterizing PASC.

studies.title: From COVID-19-Associated Acute Kidney Injury to Long-Term Kidney Dysfunction: Recovery Phenotypes, Risk Stratification, and Post-COVID Renal Surveillance.
studies.authors: Madkhali, Faisal, Mjery, Yahia A, Mohrag, Mostafa, Abdulrasak, Mohammed
studies.abstract: COVID-19-associated acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in severe disease, but its long-term kidney implications are heterogeneous and incompletely defined. To synthesize recovery phenotypes and longitudinal outcomes, reconcile conflicting evidence on whether COVID-associated AKI differs from other-cause AKI, and set out implications for surveillance and management. The evidence base was assembled through a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE search for COVID-19 and kidney dysfunction (January 2020 to August 2026), hand-searching of reference lists, and direct retrieval of pivotal longitudinal cohorts and clinical practice guidelines. Longitudinal cohorts and comparative studies were prioritized. AKI severity, duration, kidney replacement therapy, lower baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and incomplete early recovery consistently identify patients at greatest risk. Longitudinal studies disagree on whether COVID-AKI confers more risk than AKI from other illnesses: early cohorts reported steeper eGFR loss, whereas a later 9624-patient cohort found lower adjusted major adverse kidney events. This divergence reflects differences in kidney reference point, outcome construction, ascertainment, and handling of competing death rather than genuine contradiction. Population studies show long-term kidney failure is concentrated after hospitalization and severe disease. Candidate biomarkers remain investigational. Post-COVID kidney risk is severity- and phenotype-dependent rather than universal. Follow-up is most defensible after hospitalized AKI, incomplete recovery, advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), dialysis, or transplantation and applies existing post-AKI guidance rather than a COVID-specific schedule. studies.title: Overlapping Post-COVID Conditions: A Case of Myalgic Encephalomyelitis and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome Triggered by Sequential Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Infections.
studies.authors: Mayrink Magalhães, Virgínia R, Ribeiro Oliveira, Laura A, Lourenço, Adelina J, Ribeiro Camargos, Isabela et al.
studies.abstract: The rise in post-infectious syndromes following COVID-19, such as Myalgic Encephalomyelitis/Chronic Fatigue Syndrome (ME/CFS) and Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome (POTS), has become increasingly common in clinical practice, representing an emerging clinical challenge. This case highlights a possible clinical scenario involving the interaction between sequential viral infections - such as the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) - in triggering overlapping chronic conditions. This report presents the case of a patient who developed ME/CFS and POTS following SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a prior history of EBV mononucleosis, and discusses the diagnostic, therapeutic, and pathophysiological implications. A 48-year-old woman with a history of mononucleosis in childhood developed persistent and disabling symptoms after COVID-19 in January 2022. She presented with extreme fatigue, orthostatic intolerance, paresthesia, cognitive dysfunction, and multisystem symptoms. After extensive investigation, she was diagnosed with ME/CFS (early 2023) and POTS (later that year). Mast Cell Activation Syndrome (MCAS) was considered as a hypothesis during follow-up, but objective testing was not confirmatory. Management included pharmacological therapy (including low-dose naltrexone, duloxetine, and palmitoylethanolamide (PEA)), activity adjustments (pacing), and a multidisciplinary approach, with partial and fluctuating responses. This case illustrates how viral infections such as EBV and SARS-CoV-2 may act as sequential triggers in an individual clinical trajectory compatible with the development of ME/CFS and POTS. The symptomatic overlap, the lack of readily available objective biomarkers in this patient, and the need for a predominantly clinical and functional diagnostic approach in her evaluation highlight the complexity of these conditions. This experience also underscores the importance of continued efforts in research, clinical training, and integrated care models to improve the management of patients presenting with post-COVID conditions (PCC).

studies.title: Redox shielding unlocks damage-free photopolymerization for GelMA 3D co-cultures mimicking pancreatic tumor complexity.
studies.authors: Lac, Claire, Petsophonsakul, Petnoi, Foncy, Julie, Fanjul, Marjorie et al.
studies.abstract: Developing physiologically relevant 3D tumor models is critical to study cell-stroma interactions driving cancer progression. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), pancreatic stellate cells (PSCs) are key stromal actors that acquire pro-tumoral functions upon activation into cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). We aimed to create a 3D co-culture model combining PSCs (or CAFs) and tumor organoids (or spheroids) that reproduces the tumor microenvironment while preserving the viability of fragile stroma cells. Gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) was selected as a biocompatible scaffold with mechanical properties comparable to pancreatic tissue. However, fragile stromal cells, such as PSCs, displayed extensive photopolymerization-induced cell death when embedded in GelMA, preventing long-term culture. We developed a simple preconditioning protocol with an antioxidant (N-acetylcysteine, NAC) that protects sensitive cells prior to GelMA encapsulation. This approach allowed long-term 3D culture of healthy PSCs and CAFs, alone or in co-culture with tumor spheroids or organoids. Cells self-organized, maintained physiological morphology, secreted extracellular matrix, and formed stromal networks around tumor structures, closely mimicking the PDAC tissue architecture. This straightforward and reproducible approach enables sensitive stromal cells to thrive in 3D GelMA, providing a robust platform to study tumor-stroma crosstalk and to support drug testing in PDAC-relevant models.

studies.title: A comparison of health care utilization among insured working-age adults in the state of Virginia, U.S. by long COVID and disabling condition status in 2022.
studies.authors: Plante, Erica-Lyn, Brucker, Debra L
studies.abstract: Americans with disabilities experience more medical interactions and greater access barriers than those without. After the COVID-19 pandemic, Long COVID (LCOVID) emerged as a chronic condition. Few studies examine patterns among people with disabling conditions who develop LCOVID. This study compared healthcare utilization rates among individuals with and without LCOVID and/or a potentially disabling condition (PDC) among working-age adults in Virginia's insurance plans in 2022. Retrospective analysis using 2021-22 administrative claims data from Virginia's All-Payer Claims Database estimated rates of primary, emergency, and inpatient care among adults aged 18-64 with PDC(s) and LCOVID. Disabling conditions were identified using specifications from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, and LCOVID was identified using the ICD-10 code U09.9. Members were grouped by PDC/LCOVID status, sex and age. We applied regression models to estimate rates and compare differences across diagnostic groups. Among most groups, individuals with both PDCs and LCOVID had the highest rates of primary, emergency, and inpatient utilization. Those with LCOVID or PDC alone also often had higher utilization than those with neither. These findings underscore the need for accessible, cost-effective care for people with disabling conditions and Long COVID.

studies.title: Multifactorial biomarker profiles in fatigued and non-fatigued post-COVID-19 patients: insights from a one-year follow-up.
studies.authors: Barrero-Santiago, Laura, Gomes de Jesus Ferreira, Leandro, Salomão, Rebecca, da Silva Almeida, Isabella et al.
studies.abstract: To compare blood biomarkers across SARS-CoV-2 fatigue, non-fatigue, and control groups; assessed longitudinal biomarker changes; and identified genetic associations and biomarkers linked to post-COVID-19 fatigue. This longitudinal observational study followed individuals with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection over a one-year period, stratifying them into fatigue (n = 27) and non-fatigue (n = 13) groups based on the Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS). These groups were cross-sectionally compared with a non-infected control cohort (n = 27). Blood samples were collected at four time points to assess cytokines, hematological and biochemical markers, inflammatory indices, and matrix metalloproteinases. Selected functional polymorphisms were genotyped using PCR-RFLP. Group comparisons were conducted using generalized estimating equations, and genetic associations were evaluated using odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. At baseline, fatigued post-COVID participants had higher IL-6 (2.70 vs. 1.68 pg/mL, p < 0.001), IL-8 (6.09 vs. 3.68 pg/mL, p = 0.024), and hs-CRP (6.61 vs. 1.06 mg/L, p < 0.001) than controls. Across follow-up, the fatigued group showed higher IL-6 (mean difference [MD] 1.27 pg/mL, p = 0.009), IL-8 (MD 1.98 pg/mL, p = 0.017), and hs-CRP (MD 4.16 mg/L, p < 0.001) than the non-fatigued group. In exploratory genotype analyses, fatigue was associated with COMT rs4680 (OR 13.85, 95% CI 2.74-69.91), NR3C1 rs41423247 (OR 3.76, 95% CI 1.04-13.69), and MMP9 rs3918242 (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.06-0.67). Hs-CRP was significantly associated with FSS score (B = 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.21; p = 0.014). Post-COVID fatigue was associated with persistent inflammation and genetic variation, supporting a multifactorial biological basis and highlighting hs-CRP as a potential marker requiring further validation.

studies.title: Intrinsic capacity with COVID-19 infection and late complications in the older adult population.
studies.authors: Nikbakht, Hossein-Ali, Bakhtiari, Afsaneh, Tamadoni, Negar, Sivan, Manoj et al.
studies.abstract: Intrinsic capacity (IC) decline, infection susceptibility, and post-COVID sequelae in older adults, intensified by the pandemic, demand probing IC domains' infection/outcome links and population-level strategies for sustaining functional health. This cross-sectional study enrolled 600 older adults. IC was assessed using the World Health Organization's ICOPE framework. Post-COVID-19 condition was defined according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention criteria, and late complications were evaluated via the culturally adapted and validated Persian C19-YRS questionnaire. COVID-19 infection status was confirmed through polymerase chain reaction testing of nasopharyngeal swabs or serological antibody assays. Statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS Version 22, including independent t-tests, analysis of variance, and regression models. Overall, most participants demonstrated relatively preserved IC across domains, although greater variability was observed in the psychological domain. In multivariable analysis, higher scores in the psychological IC domain were independently associated with COVID-19 infection (OR = 1.04, 95% CI: 1.00-1.08). Lower cognitive and sensory IC scores were significantly associated with poorer functional ability (B = -0.35, 95% CI: -0.66 to -0.04; and B = -0.50, 95% CI: -0.90 to -0.10, respectively), while higher sensory IC scores were associated with better general health among participants with post-COVID-19 complications (B = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.01-0.47). These findings indicate meaningful associations between IC and both COVID-19 infection status and post-infectious health outcomes in older adults. Monitoring and supporting IC may be relevant for maintaining functional independence and quality of life in ageing populations during and after widespread infectious disease outbreaks.

studies.title: Syphilis in pregnancy detection rate: time series study associated with descriptive analysis by periods, Campo Grande, 2015-2023.
studies.journal: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil
studies.authors: Reis, Caroliny Oviedo Fernandes, Borges, Luciana Aparecida da Cunha, Santos-Pinto, Cláudia Du Bocage, de Oliveira, Ana Lúcia Lyrio et al.
studies.abstract: To analyze the time series and trend of the syphilis in pregnancy detection rate over nine years and the variations in clinical and epidemiological characteristics across four periods according to relevant public health events in Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul. Time series study with descriptive analysis by periods, using data from the Notifiable Diseases Information System ( A total of 2,802 cases were analyzed. An increase of 170.4% in the detection rate was observed, with a rising trend until 2018 (annual percentage change, APC 31.18%; 95% confidence interval, 95%CI 4.79; 118.80; p-value 0.017) and subsequent stabilization (APC 1.16%; 95%CI -27.24; 15.83; p-value 0.936). Regarding clinical-epidemiological characteristics, there was an increase in the frequency of latent phase, reactive treponemal tests, adequate treatment, and maternal education, and a reduction in partner treatment. During 2017-2019, there was a reduction in the use of non-treponemal tests; in 2020-2021, a decrease in Brown (Brazilian mixed race)/Black/Asian/Indigenous women; and in 2022-2023, an increase in prenatal care visits and late diagnoses. The syphilis in pregnancy detection rate increased until 2018 and remained stable thereafter. Changes in clinical and epidemiological characteristics reflect variations in the care context, with advances in prenatal care, but persistence of weaknesses in the timely diagnosis and treatment of partners. Estudio de serie temporal con análisis descriptivo por períodos, utilizando datos del Sistema de Información de Enfermedades de Notificación Obligatoria ( Se analizaron 2.802 casos. Se observó un aumento del 170,4% en la tasa de detección, con tendencia creciente hasta 2018 (variación porcentual anual, VPA 31,18%; intervalo de confianza del 95%, IC95% 4,79; 118,80; p-valor 0,017) y estabilización posterior (VPA 1,16%; IC95% -27,24; 15,83; p-valor 0,936). En las características clínico-epidemiológicas, se verificó un aumento de la frecuencia de la fase latente, de la positividad de las pruebas treponémicas, del tratamiento adecuado y de la escolaridad de la mujer, y una reducción del tratamiento de las parejas. En el período 2017–2019, hubo una reducción en el uso de pruebas no treponémicas; en 2020–2021, una reducción en el uso por parte de mujeres mestizas (pardas)/negras/amarillas/indígenas; y en 2022–2023, un aumento en las consultas de control prenatal y en los diagnósticos tardíos. La tasa de detección de sífilis durante el embarazo aumentó hasta 2018 y se mantuvo estable posteriormente. Los cambios en las características clínicas y epidemiológicas reflejan variaciones en el contexto asistencial, con avances en el cuidado prenatal, pero la persistencia de fragilidades en el diagnóstico oportuno y en el tratamiento de las parejas.

studies.title: Strong Protein Responses to Acute Infection Control General Post-Viral Sequelae and SARS-CoV-2-specific Neurocognitive Sequelae.
studies.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
studies.authors: Liou, Theodore G, Andrews, Ryan J, Battey, Heather S, Bass, Brenda L et al.
studies.abstract: After serious infections, many survivors fully recover while others face persistent symptoms including neurocognitive dysfunction, cardiopulmonary instabilities and disabling fatigue, classified broadly as Post-Acute Infection Syndromes (PAIS). Post-Acute Sequelae of COVID19 (PASC) is one special case. To test whether acute infection initiates PAIS, we analyzed proteins in 173 saliva samples collected during severe respiratory viral infections and tracked patient outcomes for five years. We discovered 44 proteins, all derived from interferon stimulated genes, that respond strongly to acute infection. Rates of post-acute syndromes were similar regardless of infection, but the types of Sequelae differed by virus. High expression of 19 proteins predict low General Sequelae rates across all viruses. High expression of 23 overlapping proteins predict low Neurocognitive Sequelae rates only with SARS-CoV-2 infections. We propose that low expressions of these proteins, which control viral replication, innate immunity, and secondary autoimmunity, combine to precipitate PAIS and PASC. Acute viral infections elicit interferon stimulated gene (ISG) protein responses.23 ISG proteins prevent post-infection General Sequelae for all viral infections.19 ISG proteins prevent post-infection Neurocognitive Sequelae only with SARS-CoV-2.Poor protein responses induce distinct post-viral syndromes with or without COVID19.

studies.title: Prevalence and Trends of Post-COVID-19 Sequelae Among U.S. Adults With Prior COVID-19 Infection, 2022-2024.
studies.authors: Bhargava, Ashish, Szpunar, Susan
studies.abstract: Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC) affect a substantial proportion of U.S. adults, involving multiple organ systems and resulting in significant disability and diminished quality of life. Population-level PASC estimates include individuals without prior COVID-19 infection and therefore do not accurately reflect postinfection risk required for effective risk stratification. We estimated the prevalence and trends of PASC among U.S. adults with prior COVID-19. We analyzed data from the National Health Interview Survey (2022-2024), a nationally representative survey of the U.S. civilian noninstitutionalized population. Adults reporting prior COVID-19 infection were asked whether they ever experienced symptoms lasting ≥3 months that were not present before infection; those answering yes were classified as having PASC. Weighted analyses accounted for the complex survey design. Among 42,872 adults with prior COVID-19, 6,822 reported symptoms lasting three months or longer, indicating PASC. Prevalence declined from 19.7% in 2022 to 15.1% in 2023 and 13.7% in 2024 (P<0.001 for 2022 vs subsequent years). Despite this decline, more than 21 million U.S. adults reported having experienced PASC in 2023 and 2024. Prevalence was higher among women and adults aged 35-64 years than among men and younger or elderly individuals. A lower prevalence was observed among Asian adults, whereas a higher prevalence was noted among American Indian, Alaska Native, and multiracial adults. Despite declining prevalence, PASC remains common among U.S. adults with prior COVID-19. These nationally representative postinfection estimates provide clinically relevant risk information to guide patient counseling, health system planning, and ongoing surveillance.

studies.title: Economic Burden of Post-COVID Syndrome in Germany Between 2021 and 2025: A Statutory Health Insurance Claims Data Analysis.
studies.journal: Journal of health economics and outcomes research
studies.authors: Gensorowsky, Daniel, Fröling, Emma, Braegelmann, Kylie, Diekmannshemke, Jana et al.
studies.abstract: Evidence on the economic burden of post-COVID syndrome in Germany remains limited. This study quantifies post-COVID-associated healthcare resource utilization (HCRU), sick leave, and costs. To compare HCRU, sick leave, and costs borne by the statutory health insurance (SHI) among incident pediatric and adult post-COVID patients with matched post-COVID-free controls. This retrospective cohort study analyzed an anonymized German SHI claims database provided by GWQ ServicePlus AG. The observation period spanned October 2021 to June 2025 and included all individuals with incident COVID-19 diagnosis until September 2024. Incident post-COVID was defined as the first ICD-10-GM code (U07.4!; U09.9!) recorded ≥90 days after first COVID-19 diagnosis. Post-COVID cases were exactly matched 1:2 to post-COVID-free COVID-19 controls by calendar quarter of incident COVID-19 diagnosis, acute severity, cohort entry quarter, 5-year birth interval, sex, and Elixhauser Comorbidity Index. We estimated mean differences in HCRU, sick leave, and direct SHI-borne costs per case. Rate ratios of HCRU, sick leave, and costs per person-year were estimated using Poisson (HCRU/sick leave) and linear (costs) regression. Analyses covered 365-day, 730-day, and any follow-up period. We matched 25 485 identified post-COVID cases with 49 671 controls. Matched cases and controls were comparable in age, sex, and comorbidities. Overall, during 365 days of follow-up, post-COVID patients showed higher HCRU and sick leave rates across all sectors, especially sick leave days. Mean differences per case were greatest for sick leave days (365 days: +27 days) and outpatient physician contacts (365 days: 6.9 contacts). HCRU and sick leave rates remained significantly increased over extended follow-up periods. Total SHI-borne costs per person-year were higher among post-COVID patients across all follow-up periods (all Documented post-COVID was associated with a substantial and sustained economic burden on the German healthcare system and society. Targeted strategies are needed to mitigate potential long-term impacts on HCRU and labor productivity.

studies.title: Post-COVID syndrome's impact on sex life - results from a cross-sectional study.
studies.authors: Schröder, Dominik, Schmachtenberg, Tim, Heinemann, Stephanie, Müllenmeister, Christina et al.
studies.abstract: Having a satisfying sexual life is important to many people and impairment of sexual function is often perceived as a burden. This study investigates the self-perceived impairments to sex life in adults with Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) and factors that are associated with impaired sex life. A cross-sectional online survey of people with PCS and without PCS was conducted in Northern Germany. Sex life impairments were assessed using item 8 (frequency and quality of sex life) of the Index for the Assessment of Health Impairments (IMET), scored from 0 (no impairment) to 10 (no activity possible). Scores were analyzed as a continuous outcome because no validated cut-offs have been established for this individual item. Linear regression models were used to adjust for sociodemographic factors as well as medical and mental health conditions. Sample weighting for age and gender was applied in sensitivity analyses to adjust for a representative sample of people with PCS. A total of 892 participants were included, with 67.8% (n = 605) reporting PCS. Persons with PCS reported significantly higher sex life impairments (mean score 4.62) compared to those without PCS (mean score 2.58, p < 0.001). The regression model confirmed that PCS was associated with sex life impairments (β = 1.16, p < 0.001). No significant correlation was found between sex life impairments and the symptom duration symptoms or the respondents´ gender. Impaired sex life is a significant concern for PCS patients, that warrants attention from healthcare providers. Our findings highlight the importance of addressing sex life impairments in the care of people with PCS.

studies.title: Scavenger Receptor Class B Type 1 Mediated Transport Enables Delivery Across Capillarized Liver Sinusoids in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis.
studies.authors: Yuan, Ruyan, Zhang, Jiamin, Huang, Yamei, Meng, Yiyang et al.
studies.abstract: Liver fibrosis in metabolic dysfunction associated steatohepatitis (MASH) lacks effective therapies, in part because therapeutic agents poorly penetrate the capillarized sinusoidal endothelium. As fibrosis progresses, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells (LSECs) become defenestrated and restrict trans-sinusoidal exchange, thereby limiting drug access to hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) within the perisinusoidal space. Here, we developed a lipoprotein mimetic liposomal nanocarrier, SV@SRB-Lip, to exploit scavenger receptor class B type 1 (SR-B1)-associated transendothelial transport across capillarized LSECs and enhance downstream delivery toward HSC-associated fibrotic regions. SV@SRB-Lip was engineered as a simvastatin loaded liposomal platform incorporating an ApoA-I-mimetic SRB peptide, an MMP-responsive linker, and a vitamin A modified lipid moiety. SV@SRB-Lip promoted transport across the LSEC monolayer in vitro, and this effect was reduced by SR-B1 silencing, supporting the involvement of SR-B1-associated endothelial transport. In MASH mice, SV@SRB-Lip enhanced hepatic delivery and distributed toward HSC associated fibrotic regions. The MMP-responsive design increased the relative accessibility of vitamin A within the fibrotic microenvironment, supporting downstream HSC associated uptake. As a result, SV@SRB-Lip increased hepatic simvastatin accumulation, suppressed HSC activation and collagen deposition, and improved MASH associated fibrosis. These findings suggest that SR-B1-associated endothelial transport can be harnessed to overcome the capillarized sinusoidal barrier and improve antifibrotic nanomedicine delivery in MASH.

studies.title: Central Nervous System Alterations in Individuals with Long COVID: A Systematic Review.
studies.journal: Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical
studies.authors: Moraes, Janaina Ferreira de, Souza, Paulo Henrique Leite, Andrade, Michele Lacerda de, Dias, Raphael Mendes Ritti et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (post-COVID-19 condition) has been associated with persistent neurological and cognitive symptoms, suggesting possible central nervous system involvement beyond the acute phase of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection. A systematic review of articles published up to April 2026 was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines, and observational studies evaluating neurophysiological, structural, and functional alterations in individuals with long COVID were analyzed. Forty-two studies with substantial variability in design and methods were included; thus, the findings were synthesized narratively. The evidence indicates heterogeneous yet recurrent alterations in the central nervous system of individuals with lonf COVID, including impaired cortical excitability, abnormal cerebral oscillatory activity across multiple frequency bands, changes in functional connectivity, and structural abnormalities in neural networks. Some studies also reported imbalances in excitatory-inhibitory neurotransmission and biomarkers suggestive of neuroinflammation or axonal injury. These neurophysiological and structural alterations were commonly associated with persistent fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and brain fog. However, the available evidence is limited by important methodological issues, including substantial heterogeneity in study populations, assessment techniques, and reported outcomes; the observational design also limited the strength of the conclusions. Taken together, the current evidence suggests a persistent and multifactorial central nervous system dysfunction in long COVID. However, definitive conclusions remain limited, and well-designed prospective longitudinal studies using standardized methods are needed to clarify the mechanisms, duration, and clinical relevance of these alterations.

studies.title: Prevalence of alpha-synuclein seeding activity in the Olfactory Mucosa following SARS-CoV-2 infection: results from a pilot study.
studies.authors: Heim, Beatrice, Seppi, Klaus, De Cleene, Nicolas, Bongianni, Matilde et al.
studies.abstract: Olfactory dysfunction (OD) is a hallmark of SARS-CoV-2-infection where it is believed to result from neuroinflammation induced by viral invasion via the olfactory mucosa (OM). Hyposmia also affects the majority of patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) where it is caused by α-synuclein (aSyn) pathology in the olfactory system, and aSyn-seeding-activity can be detected in the OM using aSyn-seeding-amplification-assays (aSyn-SAA). The present pilot study aimed to investigate whether SARS-CoV-2-infection induces local aSyn-misfolding and -aggregation in OM samples using aSyn-SAA. We conducted an observational study including PD patients (n = 51), individuals with a history of documented symptomatic SARS-CoV-2-infection (post-COVID; n = 95), and healthy controls (HC; n = 42). Post-COVID-participants were stratified based on persistent OD (COVID+OD; n = 42) or normal olfaction (COVID-OD; n = 53) using Sniffin'-Sticks-Identification (SSI) and -Discrimination (SSD) tests. OM samples were obtained by ENT specialists and analyzed by aSyn-SAA at the University of Verona. Clinical phenotyping included MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, and the Innsbruck-RBD-Inventory. OM-SAA positivity rates were significantly different between PD and both post-COVID-participants and HCs (80.4% vs 24.2% vs 11.9%; p < 0.001). Within the post-COVID-group, positivity rates were higher in COVID+OD vs COVID-OD (35.7% vs 15.1%; p = 0.030), and COVID+OD differed from HC (p = 0.030), while COVID-OD did not (p = 0.65). Among post-COVID-participants, aSyn-SAA positivity was associated with lower SSI (p = 0.007) and SSD (p < 0.001) scores, but not with MDS-UPDRS, MoCA, or RBD measures. OM-SAA-positivity was enriched among individuals with persistent post-COVID-OD and correlated with olfactory impairment. These findings support the hypothesis that neuroinflammation following SARS-COV-2-infection might promote local aSyn-aggregation. The biological and prognostic relevance of OM-SAA positivity is unknown and needs further prospective investigation.

studies.title: A narrative review of stem cell-based therapy for fibrosing interstitial lung diseases: clinical evidence and translational perspectives.
studies.authors: Li, Zhengnan, Geng, Lei, Li, Wei, Wang, Xiujuan et al.
studies.abstract: Fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (F-ILD) are a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by pulmonary interstitial fibrosis and inflammation. Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is the most common and severe form of F-ILD. Regulator-approved anti-fibrotic drugs, such as pirfenidone and nintedanib, delay rather than reverse disease progression, so the threat of eventual respiratory failure remains. While lung transplantation is an option that can prolong survival for end-stage IPF, its clinical application is greatly restricted by donor shortages, surgical risks, and postoperative complications. Stem cell therapies, and particularly treatments based on mesenchymal stromal/stem cells (MSCs) and their derivatives, have brought new hope for the management of F-ILD due to their immune regulatory, anti-inflammatory, and anti-fibrotic capabilities. A search was conducted to identify relevant articles in the PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Internet and Wanfang Data from inception to 31st May 2026. This review summarizes the mechanistic overview of stem cell-based therapeutic strategies for F-ILD, safety profiles and therapeutic potentials of various stem cells for the treatment of IPF and other F-ILDs, with an emphasis on stem cell types and delivery routine. This article also discusses the challenges and limitations of stem cell-based therapies, highlighting the need for further clinical studies with standardized efficacy endpoints to validate their effectiveness.

studies.title: Long COVID is associated with lipoxygenase-catalyzed metabolism of essential polyunsaturated fatty acids.
studies.authors: Moss, M Elizabeth, Pons, Stephanie, Tavares, Luciana P, Tang, Yan et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID (LC) represents a failure of healthy resolution mechanisms for inflammation after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Dietary essential polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) and their downstream metabolites can orchestrate inflammation resolution, suggesting these pathways may be altered in LC. In this study, plasma samples from two independent participant cohorts totaling 106 participants (designated by chart review as LC or Recovered) were collected longitudinally in the 12 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection and analyzed by mass spectrometry for targeted PUFA metabolites. In the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection, upregulation of PUFA metabolites downstream of 12-lipoxygenase was associated with later development of LC. In the months following infection, LC participants displayed uncoupling of PUFA-related lipid metabolism and altered lipoxygenase-driven metabolism over time compared to recovered participants. These results provide new mechanistic insights for the development of LC and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for this prevalent and debilitating disorder.

studies.title: Test-retest reliability and interpretability of Long COVID Burden Index: A prospective observational study.
studies.journal: Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy
studies.authors: Yamada, Gen, Iwamoto, Noriko, Miyamori, Daisuke, Suzuki, Michiyo et al.
studies.abstract: The Long COVID Burden Index (LCBI) is an 11-item patient-reported outcome measure developed to assess the burden of long COVID symptoms on daily life. Although its cross-sectional validity and internal consistency have been demonstrated, its test-retest reliability, measurement error, and minimal important change (MIC) have not yet been evaluated. We conducted a longitudinal postal survey among adults with a history of COVID-19 hospitalization. The LCBI was administered at the initial survey, 2-week follow-up, and 3-month follow-up. Test-retest reliability was assessed among participants who completed the initial and 2-week surveys and reported no change on a 7-point global rating of change question. Measurement error was evaluated using the standard error of measurement (SEM) and the smallest detectable change (SDC) was calculated. The MIC was estimated at 3 months by using anchor-based methods: the mean change method, receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, and predictive modeling. Among 1031 potential participants, 301 provided valid responses at the initial survey, 258 at the 2-week follow-up, and 208 at the 3-months follow-up. The intraclass correlation coefficient for the LCBI total score was 0.78 (95% confidence interval, 0.72-0.83). The SEM and SDC were 3.26 and 9.04 points, respectively. The MIC estimates ranged from 1.73 to 2.91 points across methods. The LCBI showed good test-retest reliability. A reduction of approximately 2-3 points may represent a minimal important improvement. However, this change is below the SDC and does not provide definitive evidence of change beyond measurement error.

studies.title: Protective Effect of COVID-19 Vaccination on Post-Infection Visuospatial Deficits.
studies.journal: Revista brasileira de psiquiatria (Sao Paulo, Brazil : 1999)
studies.authors: da Silva, Lucas Gomes, Fini, Bruna Carmeni Di, Oliveira, Jordano César Milagres, Rosa, Daniela Valadão et al.
studies.abstract: COVID-19 has been associated with persistent cognitive deficits months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Vaccination reduces severe disease, but its effect on post-infection cognition remains uncertain. We evaluated whether COVID-19 vaccination attenuates cognitive deficits after SARS-CoV-2. We assessed 237 adults with COVID-19 and 105 controls. Patients were grouped by vaccination status at infection (vaccinated n=87; unvaccinated n=150). The neuropsychological assessment covered language, visuospatial ability, visual memory, verbal memory, attention, executive functions, and working memory. Group differences were tested with Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA with Holm-corrected post hoc comparisons, adjusting for education. Significant group differences were observed in visuospatial ability and visual memory, assessed with the Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test (Copy, Immediate and Delayed Recall) (all p < 0.001). The vaccinated group outperformed the unvaccinated group (p = 0.022) on visuospatial performance. The Rey-Osterrieth Complex Figure Test Copy did not differ significantly among participants vaccinated with CoronaVac, AstraZeneca, or Pfizer. The findings suggest that COVID-19 vaccination may mitigate post-infection visuospatial deficits, reinforcing the importance of immunization in preventing cognitive sequelae associated with the disease.

studies.title: Blood biomarkers of long COVID: A cross-sectional evaluation of key cytokines and the coordination of inflammation.
studies.authors: Thomas, Callum, Ashton, Ruth E, Pretorius, Etheresia, Owen, Rebecca et al.
studies.abstract: Long COVID is a complex pathophysiological condition linked to a heterogenous symptom profile. Dysregulation of 1) immunological and inflammatory responses, 2) endothelial/vascular function, and 3) metabolic and clotting processes have been identified; however, there remains a lack of clinically validated diagnostic biomarkers. The study aim was to investigate dysregulation of cytokines, chemokines and growth factors in confirmed Long COVID cases grouped by disease severity. One-hundred-and-twenty-seven participants provided venous blood samples for cytokine profiling utilising Luminex assays. Participants were grouped into those with no knowledge of SARS-CoV-2 infection (n = 21), acute infection within 3-months (n = 22), spontaneous resolvers (>3-months, n = 21) and those with confirmed Long COVID (n = 63). Long COVID severity was grouped according to the post-COVID-19 functional status (PCFS) and defined as those with negligible (4A; n = 9), mild (4B; n = 20), moderate (4C; n = 24), and severe limitations (4D; n = 10). Cytokines were assessed for normality using Shapiro-Wilk tests and differences measured between groups using Kruskal-Wallis tests. Pairwise correlation and principal component analysis were performed. Interleukin-12 (p40/p70) was 22% greater in the Long COVID group (Median [IQR]: 58 [49] pg/mL, p = 0.046) and 30% greater in the acutely infected group (64 [36] pg/mL; p = 0.039) against non-infected controls (45 [25] pg/mL). Following PCFS classification, fibroblast growth factor-basic was 25% lower in Long COVID 4B versus spontaneous resolvers (24 [7] vs. 32 [24] pg/mL; p = 0.025). Pairwise correlation differences demonstrated that three Long COVID subgroups had strong, positive associations between cytokines when compared to non-infected controls; however, PCA was unable to determine any coordinated cytokine variation that was group specific. Elevated interleukin-12 (p40/p70) and reduced basic fibroblast growth factor suggest persistent immune activation and possible subgroup-specific Long COVID; however, these findings were marginally significant and exploratory. A coordinated but partial immunological/inflammatory profile may exist in some of those with Long COVID, suggesting a rationale for subgrouping upon a biological, rather than self-report basis but larger longitudinal studies are required to confirm this hypothesis.
